items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: her husband, who was R. C. Reynaud, Ralph Reynaud, was the principal of the school in Lake Charles that I attended

ctx.x: Well, I guess I can say, Pat, really I can hardly remember when I couldn't play music, because as I say, it was a natural thing with me, although I did study music, I have studied. We had instruments around the house. We had an old broken down phonograph, you know, with the horn, the big horn, we had that. And by my dad being a musician, and they used to play. He and, used to be another gentlemen who used to come around the house, he was a guitar player, and he and my father used to just sit and just play, and…

of the other old guys would come by and they would just sit. That was the way they entertained themselves, you know, they would just sit and play, and we always had instruments around the house, and I just took a liking and a love of the piano, and my feet couldn't even reach the pedals, and I could get there and pick out certain things, you know, and my folks, my folks saw to it, naturally, by my mother being home all the time, and of course daddy was at work, but they both knew, you know, they thought I had…

She egged me on and encouraged me on, and she showed me all the -- whatever she could. I shall never forget one time at a graduation exercise, she had me to play the 'Blue Danube Waltz' behind a choral group. Yes, and I was very young
